title: Expert review of the benchmark's labels (kit built)
request: Two reviewers should label a sample of benchmark cases (dev and test) without seeing the expected decisions, and the agreement between them and with the benchmark should be measured; labels corrected on dev, and the sealed set frozen after review (a new version if a test label changes, never an edit). The reviewers are not yet named, so build the kit that does not need them.
spec: A blank form per reviewer for a stratified sample; agreement and Cohen's kappa between the reviewers and with the benchmark; disagreements recorded; a changed sealed label makes a new benchmark version.
plan: Write dclab_rnd/agent_eval/review.py: export writes a blank form per reviewer for a stratified sample of dev and test cases (one row per column: name, kind, missing share, distinct count, three values; the reviewer fills keep_out, usable, time or group) under anonymous references, with a key only the owner keeps.
agreement reads the two returned forms and reports agreement and Cohen's kappa between the reviewers and with the benchmark, every disagreement with all three views, and the cases both confirm.
Write tests; review with the other kits; fix the two findings on the form and the agreement; commit.

decisions.decision: Cases appear under anonymous references in an order unrelated to the benchmark's, with the key kept by the owner.
decisions.why: A case's name or position would tell the reviewer which trap was planted.

decisions.decision: A form or a key is never overwritten.
decisions.why: A reviewer's returned answers are evidence; regenerating the form could silently change the sample.

change: New dclab_rnd/agent_eval/review.py (export and agreement) and tests/test_label_review.py.

findings.defect: The form's column order showed which column was planted.
findings.scenario: Every generator appends the planted column last, so after a base's shared columns the last row was always the added one (for example a refund paid after the outcome, an exit rating, a claim number); the reviewer could also diff cases of one base.
findings.cause: Columns were listed in table order.
findings.fix: Shuffle the columns inside each case with a seeded generator keyed by the reference; mention the repeated bases in the protocol.
findings.impact: A reviewer could tell which column was planted just by looking at the last row of each case, so their 'independent' labels would agree with the benchmark by construction, and the review meant to validate the labels would have validated nothing.
findings.open: Several cases come from the same base table, so a reviewer can still compare cases of one base to spot the added column; the protocol names it, the form cannot prevent it.

findings.defect: A case could be 'confirmed by both' with its planted column never reviewed.
findings.scenario: Both reviewers fill only the clean columns of a missing-is-outcome case and leave the planted score blank; it lands in the confirmed cases, because agreement was built only from rows both reviewers decided.
findings.cause: A blank was silently ignored rather than counted as undecided.
findings.fix: A case is confirmed only when every benchmark-labelled column is decided by both reviewers and matches; per-case coverage and undecided labelled columns are reported.
findings.impact: A case where both reviewers skipped the planted column would be reported as confirmed by both, so the agreement figures would overstate how much of the benchmark's labels experts had actually checked.

outcome: Kit built (c291a1b), open on two reviewers: export and agreement are tested, including chance-corrected kappa and refusal of a wrong word; no review has run.
lessons: A blind review form leaks through order and position as easily as through names; shuffle within each case.
A blank is not agreement: confirmation must require the labelled items to be decided.
risks: Any order or pattern in the form (the planted column last, repeated bases) lets a reviewer see the answer, which defeats a blind review.
A blank must count as undecided, never as agreement, or coverage is overstated.
Agreement needs chance correction (Cohen's kappa); raw agreement on mostly clean columns looks high by default.
A changed sealed label must create a new benchmark version, never an edit of the frozen one.
The kit cannot be proven until two named reviewers use it; the package stays open on people, not code.
